about: Dashed and dotted strokes (docs/dev/handwriting.md 'Dash'). A stroke's `dash` is 'dashed' or 'dotted' (absent: solid); the pattern is never stored but derived from the stroke's nominal `size` at render time by one table in two languages, DASH in frontend/src/ink/ink.js and ink.py: dashed on = off = 2 * size; dotted on = 0.1 * size, off = 2 * size; round caps on every surface, so a dotted constant-width stroke's dot is a round-capped dash 0.1 * size long. `patterns` rows give (dash, size, whether the stroke carries w) and expect `on` / `off` in points (null for solid), `dasharray`, the string a stroked SVG path gets as stroke-dasharray and a constant-width live stroke as setLineDash (null when the stroke is a filled outline, i.e. carries w, or is solid), and `pdf`, the operator pdf_path_ops writes before the stroke's path ('[] 0 d' follows it; null for solid). The phase is 0 at the first sample of every stroke and of every piece the partial eraser leaves, and the pattern multiplies `size`, never the drawn width: a 2 pt pen's dashes are 4 pt long whatever w says. A CONSTANT-WIDTH stroke (highlighter, ballpoint, pen false) keeps its stroked centreline and gets the dasharray. A PRESSURE stroke (w present) is cut by arc length into on-runs [k * (on + off), k * (on + off) + on) clipped to the stroke's length, each run the samples whose arc lies inside it plus a sample lerped at each boundary (x, y, p, t, w linear in the arc; a and z copied from the sample before the boundary), each run outlined on its own (perfect-freehand with last: true, so each dash has round ends, run at ten times the page's scale with a midpoint added to a two-sample run, so a dash shorter than 3 pt or of two samples still draws its width) and the outlines concatenated into one filled path; a run of zero length is skipped. `runs` holds such a stroke: three samples along x with rising pressure, size 2, w = 1 + (p - 0.5), and the expected runs with their arc interval and their samples after lerping (to three decimals). A DOTTED pressure stroke emits one circle per on-run, centred on the point at the run's middle arc (k * (on + off) + on / 2, clipped to the length) with diameter size * w there; `dots` holds the same stroke dotted. frontend/tests/ink.test.mjs checks dashArray / strokePath / dashRuns against every row; backend/tests/test_shared_fixtures.py checks dash_pattern, to_svg's stroke-dasharray and pdf_path_ops' d operator against `patterns`, and the server's run boundaries (used by the pencil's opacity bands and the dashed outline helper) against `runs`.

patterns.note: a dashed 2 pt ballpoint: 4 on, 4 off
a dashed 14 pt highlighter: 28 on, 28 off
a dotted 2 pt ballpoint: a 0.2 pt dash with round caps every 4.2 pt
a dashed 2 pt pressure pen: the same 4 / 4 by arc length, cut into outlined runs, so no dasharray; the PDF path writer still writes the pattern around its mean-width centreline
a dotted 3 pt brush pen: circles of diameter size * w every 6.3 pt

runs.note: a 10 pt dashed pressure stroke of size 2: runs [0, 4) and [8, 10]; the boundary at arc 4 lies 0.8 of the way from the first to the second sample, the one at arc 8 0.6 of the way from the second to the third

dots.note: the same stroke dotted: on 0.2, off 4, a dot at the middle of each on-run, 0.1, 4.3 and 8.5 pt along, with the diameter size * w there
